newsitem.title: LEBANON: Bank of Lebanon weekly CDs not issued.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Lebanon weekly CDs not issued.

text.p: There were no offers for Bank of Lebanon's weekly issue of certificates of deposit on Thursday, a central bank source said.
The source said investors were instead buying two-year treasury bills at 20.04 percent per annum.
"Everyone is rushing to buy two years T-bills that carry high yields," the source said.
The 45-day and 60-day CDs currently yield 12.25 percent and 13 percent .
The bank said on Monday its latest T-bill issue dated December 19 raised 428.3 billion Lebanese pound, of which two year bills totalled 222.3 billion.
It was the fourth time that the central bank has failed to make a weekly CD issue due to lack of market interest since it introduced the paper in November 1994.
Last week, the bank issued 60-day CDs dated December 20 worth two billion Lebanese pounds at 13 percent annual interest. It said it made no sales of its 45-day CDs carrying a 12.25 percent per annum.
